parole.significato: cobra (venomous snake from certain genera of the family Elapidae, especially of the genus Naja)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Portuguese cobra, from Old Galician-Portuguese coobra, from Latin colubra.

parole.significato: a caste, hereditary Indian socio-religious class (except the 'unclean' lowest) (depreciated in specialist usage)
parole.testo: From Portuguese casta (“lineage, race”), from the feminine of casto (“pure, chaste”), from Latin castus (“pure, clean”). Cognate with Danish, Norwegian (see below), German Kaste, English caste, French caste etc.
Possibly borrowed from Portuguese percinta, from Latin praecingō, from prae- + cingō.
Borrowed from Portuguese tronco (“block, prison, trunk”), from Latin truncus (“trunk”).

parole.significato: a zebra, a black-and-white striped equid of the genus Equus: Equus zebra, Equus quagga or Equus grevyi
parole.testo: Borrowed from Portuguese zebra, from Old Galician-Portuguese enzebro, ezebra, azebra (“wild ass”), from earlier cebrario (882), ezebrario (897), from Vulgar Latin *eciferus, from Latin equiferus (“wild horse”). The second sense is a shortening of zebrapad.
